chunks: He has advised you to exercise fear and has made it the highest point of His pleasure and all that He requires from His creatures. You should therefore fear Allāh, who is such that you are as though just in front of Him, and your forelocks are in His grip, and your change of position is in His control. If you conceal a matter, He will know of it. If you disclose a matter, He will record it. For this He has appointed honoured guards (angels) who do not omit any rightful matter nor include anything incorrect.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean to fear God according to the exhortation in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) defines Taqwa (piety) as the ultimate objective of divine pleasure, linking it to the concept of divine surveillance (Muraqabah). He elaborates on God's omnipresence and omniscience, noting that He knows what is concealed and records what is disclosed, with appointed angels ensuring that nothing is lost or recorded incorrectly. This description of divine oversight serves as a practical spiritual discipline for believers, encouraging mindfulness of God in both private and public spheres.
